{{nihongo|'''Anazawa Tenjinsha'''|穴澤天神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Musashi Province]].

'''Anazawa Tenjin Shrine''' (あなざわてんじんしゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yanokuchi (Inagi City)}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inagi City}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokyo Metropolis}}. It is identified with “Anazawa Shrine of Tama District, Musashi Province” listed in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. Its former shrine rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gōsha}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
'''Primary deity'''
* {{ill|Sukunabikona|ca|Sukunabikona|fr|Sukunabikona|it|Sukuna-hikona|ja|スクナビコナ|ko|스쿠나비코나|mni|ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯅꯕꯤꯀꯣꯅ|pl|Sukunabikona|pt|Sukunahikona|simple|Sukunabikona|sv|Suku-Na-Bikona|zh|少彥名|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}}{{sfn|Tokyo Metropolitan Shrine Association}}
: Although the current primary enshrined deity is Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto, there are differing opinions; it is also thought that originally the local tutelary deity of the area (the Anazawa deity) may have been worshipped instead.
'''Associated deities'''
* Kan-shin ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sugawara no Michizane}}){{sfn|Tokyo Metropolitan Shrine Association}}{{sfn|Edo Meisho Zue|1927|p=435}}
: In the 7th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Genroku}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=1694}}), the enshrined deity of Tenman Shrine was merged.
* Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto{{sfn|Tokyo Metropolitan Shrine Association}}
: In the 7th year of Taishō (1918), the enshrined deity of Kuniyasu Shrine was merged.

=== Subordinate shrines ===
* Inari Shrine
* Shinmei Shrine
* Sannō Shrine
* Benten Shrine
: Until the Edo period, Buddhist statues such as Daikokuten and Bishamonten were placed at the entrance of the cave{{sfn|Newly Compiled Musashi Fudoki, Yanokuchi Village}}, but in the 4th year of Meiji (1871) they were relocated to the former bettō temple, Ikō-ji{{sfn|Edo Meisho Zue|1927|p=435}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Benten Cave}})<ref>[https://www.city.inagi.tokyo.jp/kanko/rekishi/bunkazai_note.files/BENten-DOkutsu.pdf Cultural Property Note No.45: Benten Cave] Inagi City Board of Education, accessed April 14, 2023</ref>. Today, a stone shrine remains in the cave on the left.

=== Overview ===
[[File:穴澤天神社の湧水.jpg|thumb|200px|Spring water]]
The shrine is said to have been founded in March of the 4th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Kōan}} ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=423 BC}}){{sfn|Edo Meisho Zue|1927|p=438}}. The precincts are located on the mid-slope of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tama Hills}} along the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Misawa River}}. From a cave shrine beneath the cliff directly below the precincts, spring water selected as one of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=57 Famous Springs of Tokyo}} flows forth, and there is no shortage of people who come to draw this water.

According to the “Anazawa Tenjin Engi,” in the 7th year of Genroku ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=1694}}), the local land steward Katō Tarōzaemon renovated the shrine buildings and merged Tenman Shrine. On the slope on the north side of the precincts (toward the Misawa River) there are horizontal caves where {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=stone Buddhas}} were once enshrined, but they have now been moved into the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Benten Cave}} of Ikō-ji Temple. It is unclear whether this action was the result of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=anti-Buddhist movement}}. The shrine buildings were restored in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=1986}}.

Within the precincts stands a commemorative monument honoring the achievements of the private academy “Keigi-juku” run by Kubo Zenryō, a Confucian scholar said to have named the place Inagi.

The grand annual festival is held on {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=August 25}}, during which {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Edo no Sato Kagura}} (a nationally designated {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property}}<ref>{{National Designated Cultural Properties Database|302|44|Edo no Sato Kagura}}</ref>) and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=lion dances}} (a city-designated cultural property{{sfn|Inagi City}}) are offered.

=== Access ===
* 5 minutes on foot from “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Keiō Yomiuriland Station}}” on the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Keiō Sagamihara Line}}.
* 20 minutes on foot from “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yanokuchi Station}}” on the JR {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nambu Line}}.
